The Makonde people have their traditional homeland on the Mueda Plateau in the far north of Mozambique [d74678494s11p0].
Makonde communities lived in the interior region between the Mogabo and Messalo rivers near the Mueda Plateau [d74678494s11p0].
Some Makonde tribes on the Mueda Plateau eluded external control during the early phase of colonial occupation [d74678494s11p0].

Makonde and Macua groups between the Mogabo and Messalo rivers were subject to pacification efforts around 1909–1910 during colonial expansion in the region [d74678494s11p0].
The Mueda Plateau was occupied by Portuguese forces between April and July 1917 during the Mueda Campaign of World War I [d74678494s11p0].
The district of Mueda in Cabo Delgado province had a population of 113,742 according to the 2007 census, indicating a significant contemporary population in the Makonde homeland area [d1836107s0p0].

Makonde communities occupied the Mueda Plateau in northern Mozambique during the early colonial period and some Makonde tribes eluded company control on the Mueda Plateau into the early 20th century [d74678494s11p0].
Makonde groups in northern Mozambique were located between the Mogabo and Messalo rivers and were pacified by colonial forces between 1909 and 1910 [d74678494s11p0].

Makonde tribes in the area had resisted external control into the early 20th century, prompting colonial lines of posts and pacification campaigns between 1908 and 1912 that extended into Makonde territory [d74678494s11p0].

Linguistic varieties diverge in phonology, lexicon, and grammar as part of dialectal differentiation across regions [d63630s5p0].
Geographic separation by the Ruvuma/Rovuma border and district boundaries contributes to local isolation of speech communities in Cabo Delgado and Mtwara/Ruvuma [d1836107s0p0].

sub_answers.text:
Islamic coastal traders and European colonizers historically influenced coastal societies and exchanges along Mozambique's coast, creating long-distance trade links that involved northern Mozambique and neighboring regions [d19304s6p0].
The northern Mozambican coast and nearby Tanzanian coast form a contiguous East African coral coast with numerous bays, ports, and islands that supported maritime trade networks and regional contact [d19303s1p0].
Fringing reefs, mangroves, and many river mouths structured coastal navigation and settlement patterns that underpinned economic interactions across the border [d63539565s1p0].
Makonde wood sculpture emerged as a highly developed art form in northern Mozambique within this broader context of coastal trade and cultural contact [d19304s6p0].
